newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke says budget will aid honest election.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says budget will aid honest election.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Thursday his November budget must create the climate for an honest election in which the government would play fair with the public.
"My budget in November must create the climate for an honest election in which we play fair and straight with the public," he told the Conservative party annual conference.
"We will only cut taxes when we can afford to, and when it is good for the economy. Unaffordable tax cuts can only damage the economy."
Clarke pledged that everyone would eventually pay income tax of 20 percent, compared with a standard rate of 24 percent now.
"We will cut the basic rate rate of income tax to 20 pence in the pound. Eventually 20 pence will be the basic rate for everyone," he said.
Clarke said the government would "reduce and then abolish inheritance tax and capital gains tax," a move which the opposition Labour party said last week it would reverse.
He said government borriwng was coming down and he would ensure tight control of public spending while properly funding key services.

"We will keep inflation down below two and a half percent. Low inflation is critical to our future prosperity," Clarke added. Inflation figures released on Thursday showed core inflation edged up to 2.9 percent in September.
Clarke said he hoped to get public spending below the target of 40 percent of GDP and keep it there.
